verdicts.title: Complexity of the CNF-satisfiability problem
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: This paper is devoted to the complexity of the Boolean satisfiability problem. We consider a version of this problem, where the Boolean formula is specified in the conjunctive normal form. We prove an unexpected result that the CNF-satisfiability problem can be solved by a deterministic Turing machine in polynomial time.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract discusses the complexity of the CNF-satisfiability problem, but does not mention the relationship between the minimal number of states in a DFA and resolution proof width, which is the focus of the conjecture; the phrase 'We prove an unexpected result that the CNF-satisfiability problem can be solved by a deterministic Turing machine in polynomial time' implies a different research direction.

verdicts.title: A New Approach to Formal Language Theory by Kolmogorov Complexity
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We present a new approach to formal language theory using Kolmogorov complexity. The main results presented here are an alternative for pumping lemma(s), a new characterization for regular languages, and a new method to separate deterministic context-free languages and nondeterministic context-free languages. verdicts.title: Complexity of Networks (reprise)
verdicts.abstract_excerpt:
Network or graph structures are ubiquitous in the study of complex systems. Often, we are interested in complexity trends of these system as it evolves under some dynamic.
